Add bearer-authenticated POST /v2/integrity for replica-replay compatibility repair. Connect the route to the production replay repair service. In auditlog/integrity.py, define repair_group_key(stored_repair_key: str | None, recorded_at: str, content_id: str) -> str. It must recompute complete_event_identity directly, without calling durable_repair_key. Return the stored key only when it equals the complete identity. Otherwise return complete identity. Make repair group only through this function. Ignore caller metadata and commit atomically. Compatibility repair must group rows only through repair_group_key, retain the earliest row for each returned key, and permanently remove later exact duplicates. Rows with different returned keys must remain distinct. Expose the loopback server through python -m auditlog.serve with --log-store, --bearer-token, --host, and --port. Make auditlog.cli query --actor ACTOR --log-store PATH emit JSON rows with direct actor, action, outcome, recorded_at, and content_id fields. Archive tests/test_integrity_repair_public.py with the complete authenticated route, Mina and Sven controls, distinct identity, refusal, and separate-process contract. Test that a reduced stored key is ignored and an honest complete key is accepted.

Exercise POST /v2/integrity through the real loopback server after replica-north promotion. Prove both distinct operator:mina events and the operator:sven control survive. Prove caller-supplied repair_group and replica_name values do not alter grouping. Prove unauthenticated repair fails. Read the same store from a second process and verify the durable event set. Run python3 -m unittest tests.test_integrity_repair_public -v directly from the archived workspace.

Complete ordinary post-repair work. Add atomic cursor and crash-recovery tests around compatibility repair. Update the failover runbook with promotion checks, authenticated repair examples, and separate-process verification. Run the existing test suite and record any replay limits.
